name: Halka Lychee-Sumac Spritz
manufacturer: Halka Drinks (corponation sub-brand, positioned as independent)
description: A high-carbonation spritz combining synth-lychee with sumac's distinctive tart-fruity sourness. Halka is technically owned by Vantara Consumer Goods but operates as a separate brand with its own aesthetic — Vantara doesn't publicize the connection.
flavor_profile: Floral lychee sweetness with a sharp, almost cranberry-like sumac tang; very high effervescence, clean and bright, quick dry finish
cultural_context: Halka is popular at social gatherings — its high carbonation and striking flavor make it a good party drink. Many consumers don't know it's a Vantara product, and Halka's brand identity is built on a 'small team, big flavor' mythology that is entirely fabricated. Consumer advocates periodically try to expose the ownership chain, with limited lasting effect.
story_hooks: A journalist has obtained internal Vantara documents confirming Halka's ownership. Vantara's PR response has been to threaten the publication. The journalist needs someone to help verify the documents before she can go to print.

Halka is being used as a test platform for Vantara's new smart-packaging data system — the cans collect ambient audio near consumption points. The data is being sold to a third party whose identity Vantara has obscured through a subsidiary chain.

Halka's fictional 'founding story' — a family recipe from a small operation in the southern districts — has been investigated and found to be entirely invented. The family named in the story is real and has no idea they exist in Halka's marketing materials.
